verbalization: Selgantolimod appears to have a dual targeting relationship with the Prostaglandin E2 receptor EP4 subtype, as evidenced by its interaction with two distinct enzymes—Copper chaperone for superoxide dismutase and Triosephosphate isomerase—both of which are targeted by the Influenza B virus B/Hong Kong/259/2010 hemagglutinin antigen (MDCK cell derived, propiolactone inactivated). This suggests that Selgantolimod may act as a modulator of viral infection by targeting host cellular pathways, potentially interfering with viral replication or host cell function. The presence of a consistent pathway linking Selgantolimod to the EP4 receptor through the viral hemagglutinin antigen indicates a possible mechanism involving viral-host interactions, though the exact role of Selgantolimod in this process remains unclear. The high scores in both paths suggest a strong, biologically plausible connection, but further experimental validation is needed to confirm the direct interaction between Selgantolimod and the EP4 receptor.
